question: Which issues are growing fastest, and are any of them new?

answer.answer_markdown:
At 2026-W26, the data shows two themes emerging significantly above their expected baselines out of six tested for this week. 

**"A fraud or dispute report is met with blame, not help"** 
This issue is growing fastest relative to its baseline [c1]. In the last four weeks, we saw 5 calls versus an expected 0.6 (z=4.2). The root cause appears to be claims and fraud teams working to denial scripts with no duty to share evidence or explain the decision, leading customers to feel blamed instead of investigated.
Customers say:
* "the last representative refused to acknowledge any context or any explanation over the merchant blocking contact." [q1]
* "who told me directly that Chase was lying to us in order to stall out the window for which we would be able to open a dispute." [q2]
* "I tried to call chase customer support only to be yelled at by someone who had an accent I could not understand at all" [q3]

**"What the agent promised on my last call was never done"**
This is also emerging [c2], with 5 recent calls against an expected 1.3 (z=2.7). This problem occurs when requests are captured as free-text notes on the account rather than as work items, so nothing drives them to completion and no failure notice is sent back. 
Customers note:
* "She stated she could not guarantee that Chase would repay the fees and charges that we had to pay." [q4]
* "the account was shut down by chase bank even after I told them to leave it open so I can pay my bills" [q5]
* "I was assured multiple times that the Chase XXXX and XXXX XXXX  were investigating and would contact me with a settlement." [q6]

Both issues are currently flagged as emerging but not yet robust at 8 weeks, meaning they are relatively recent spikes rather than established long-term trends.
